text.p: These are the leading stories in Zambia's newspapers on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Three expelled leaders of the opposition Zambia Democratic Congress insist that party president Dean Mungomba has no powers to expel them.
- The ministry of information dismissed the chairman of the state-run Zambia National Broadcasting Corp board, Felix Kani.
- Police arrest 103 striking Pigott Maskew workers for unlawful assembly.
- The cash-strapped Maamba Collieries -- the country's only coal producer -- sent 200 workers on forced leave as part of measures the company is taking to avoid collapse.
- The International Finance Corp signed a deal with Zambia's Finance Bank for the support of export-oriented local enterprises.
- The Anti-Corruption Commission arrested two police officers for solicting a bribe from a motorist whose vehicle was impounded.
- A witness in an ongoing petition challenging the outcome of general elections held last November told the Supreme Court he was paid by ruling party officials to vote twice.
- A ruling party official claimed opposition leaders were planning to use former Zairean soldiers, who sought exile in Zambia, to destablise the country.
- President Frederick Chiluba left for Kinsasha on Thursday to witness the inauguration of the new president of the Democratic Republic of Congo, Laurent Kabila.
